title: Kingdom
description: A sprawling kingdom of crumbling stone and rigid tradition at the centre of the known world, divided into cantrevs and stretching from the snowbound north to the storm-battered east. It is a land of vast, lonely coach roads between isolated settlements, where the capital's reach thins with every mile. Its throne has stood empty since the royal court was killed, and a Regency governs in the crown's name while stern religious orders and ambitious upstarts carve out domains of their own. The Kingdom runs on inertia and largely ignores the rot taking hold in its forgotten corners, the Estate on its eastern coast foremost among them.
summary: The old kingdom at the centre of the world, held in regency since its court was killed, a land of lonely coach roads and provincial stagnation.

title: The Crossroads
description: A meeting of five roads on open ground, a day's ride from the Estate. Hired coachmen will not take the Old Road, so passengers are set down here to wait for the Caretaker. Cold fire-pits, a broken bench and abandoned luggage mark the waiting. The signpost at the centre carries five boards, one for each road, reading Guilt, Loathing, Failure, Regret and Disgrace. Travellers leave coins and small offerings at its base, as people still do at crossroads everywhere.
summary: A meeting of five roads where the Caretaker's coach collects those bound for the Estate; a place between places.

title: St. Martha's Reformatory
description: A grim stone structure perched on a desolate hillside. Its gray walls bear the weathering of harsh seasons, while inside, dormitories lined with iron-framed beds house troubled girls under the stern watch of the Sisters. The branding chamber remains most disturbing, its implements for 'marking the impure' surrounded by stains no amount of scrubbing can remove. Daily routines of prayer, labor, and harsh correction continue in this isolated place where the outside world's judgments cannot reach.
summary: A grim stone structure on a desolate hillside, serving as an isolated institution for troubled girls, known for its strict routines and branding chamber.

title: Woodsman's Cottage
description: A blackened foundation ringed by scorched trees, all that remains of the humble home where the Woodsman and his wife briefly gave shelter to the Runaway. The stone hearth stands amid the devastation, reaching skyward like an accusing finger. Despite years passing, no vegetation reclaims this scarred earth.
summary: A blackened foundation and scorched trees, all that remains of the humble home where the Woodsman and his wife once lived.

title: Stillbourne House
description: A great winged house of pale stone in one of the Kingdom's northern cantrevs, perfectly symmetrical, with a columned portico beneath a broad pediment and formal gardens stepping down to a river. Inside, its marble floors are polished bright, and the spotless rooms show little trace of life, save the family's portraits, hung in symmetrical rows along every wall, many of them painted very young.
summary: A pale, symmetrical winged house in the Kingdom's north, its gardens stepping down to a river.

title: The Hedge Maze
description: A hedge maze in the gardens of Stillbourne House, entered beneath an ornate stone arch, with dragons trimmed from the hedge standing guard at its turns. Flowers brought from abroad bloom along its walls. Only its outer paths are still open; the inner hedges have been left to grow together into a solid mass, sealing off its centre.
summary: A hedge maze of topiary dragons and exotic flowers, its centre sealed off by overgrown hedges.
